s0101.literal: Xijing suffered famine; an edict ordered Prince Azhiji's forces to seek food at Taiyuan.
s0101.idiomatic: With famine at Xijing, an edict sent Prince Azhiji's forces to forage at Taiyuan.

s0102.literal: Shandong suffered famine; an edict ordered that two-tenths of the wine taxes of Yidu and Jinan be used to collect grain.
s0102.idiomatic: With famine in Shandong, an edict directed that twenty percent of Yidu and Jinan wine revenues be turned into grain purchases.

s0103.literal: Winter, tenth month, wuchen new moon; an edict ordered both secretariats to report submitted matters to the Censorate.
s0103.idiomatic: On the wuchen new moon of the tenth month of winter, both secretariats were ordered to report all submitted business to the Censorate.

s0104.literal: On gengwu day, Venus transgressed You Zhifa.
s0104.idiomatic: On gengwu day Venus crossed You Zhifa (Right Law Enforcer).

s0105.literal: On guiyou day, an edict ordered that ancestral temple sacrifice prayer texts be written in the national script.
s0105.idiomatic: On guiyou day an edict required ancestral temple sacrifice prayers to be written in the national script.

s0106.literal: On yihai day, Song troops attacked Juzhou.
s0106.idiomatic: On yihai day Song forces attacked Juzhou.

s0107.literal: On yiyou day, sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0107.idiomatic: On yiyou day the court offered sacrifice at the imperial ancestral temple.

s0108.literal: On dinghai day, because of drought and locusts in the Nanjing and Henan circuits, this year's tax levies were reduced by six-tenths.
s0108.idiomatic: On dinghai day drought and locusts in the Nanjing and Henan circuits brought a sixty-percent reduction in this year's levies.

s0109.literal: Twenty-four wan jin of salt from Qing and Cang were dispatched, one hundred thousand shi of Nanjing rice were transported, and both were given to the Xiangyang army.
s0109.idiomatic: The court dispatched 240,000 jin of salt from Qing and Cang, transported 100,000 shi of Nanjing rice, and sent both to the Xiangyang army.

s0110.literal: On jichou day, an edict ordered that next year's ancestral temple sacrificial animals not use domesticated pigs but use wild boar instead, and that seasonal fruits not be bought from the market but taken from the inner garden.
s0110.idiomatic: On jichou day an edict directed that next year's temple sacrifices use wild boar instead of domestic pigs and that seasonal fruit come from the imperial gardens rather than the market.

s0111.literal: The imperial carriage returned from Shangdu.

s0112.literal: Xingzhong Superior Prefecture was reduced to a prefecture.
s0112.idiomatic: Xingzhong Superior Prefecture was downgraded to a regular prefecture.

s0113.literal: Famine relief was provided to Zilai Circuit in Shandong.
s0113.idiomatic: Famine relief was issued to Zilai circuit in Shandong.

s0114.literal: Eleventh month, renyin day; Mars transgressed the Western Rampart General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
s0114.idiomatic: On renyin day in the eleventh month Mars crossed the Western Rampart General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

s0115.literal: On renzi day, various princes made encampments throughout Hexi, and monks and common people jointly supplied provisions.
s0115.idiomatic: On renzi day various princes encamped throughout Hexi, with monks and civilians jointly supplying their needs.

s0116.literal: On dingsi day, an edict added two thousand troops; together with the armies previously dispatched the total was six thousand for garrison farming in Goryeo. Xindu and former Left Wing commander Shi Shu were both made Military Commissioners of Goryeo's Jin Prefecture and other places, granted tiger tallies, and put in charge of garrison-farming affairs.
s0116.idiomatic: On dingsi day two thousand more troops were ordered, bringing the total sent for garrison farming in Goryeo to six thousand. Xindu and former Left Wing commander Shi Shu were both appointed military commissioners of Goryeo's Jin Prefecture region, given tiger tallies, and placed in charge of garrison farming.

s0117.literal: An edict also instructed the King of Goryeo to establish a Ceremonial Protocol Office.
s0117.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the Goryeo king to establish a ceremonial protocol office.

s0118.literal: King Chen Guangbing of Annam sent envoys bearing tribute; a generous edict replied to them.
s0118.idiomatic: King Chen Guangbing of Annam sent tribute envoys and received a generous edict in reply.

s0119.literal: Famine relief was again provided to Zilai Circuit.
s0119.idiomatic: Zilai circuit received famine relief again.

s0120.literal: Intercalary month, dingmao new moon; the Goryeo crown prince Wang Sim returned, and Wang Chon was granted the Zhiyuan eighth-year calendar.
s0120.idiomatic: On the dingmao new moon of the intercalary month the Goryeo crown prince Wang Sim returned, and King Wang Chon was granted the eighth-year Zhiyuan calendar.

s0121.literal: On wuchen day, brocade woven with sun, moon, dragon, and tiger designs was forbidden, as was decorating saddles with rhinoceros horn.
s0121.idiomatic: On wuchen day brocade bearing sun, moon, dragon, and tiger motifs was banned, as was rhinoceros-horn saddle decoration.

s0122.literal: On jisi day, ten thousand ingots of paper money were given to the Hexi Branch Secretariat to meet annual expenses.
s0122.idiomatic: On jisi day the Hexi branch secretariat received ten thousand ingots of paper money for its annual expenses.

s0123.literal: Yizhou was placed under Pansha Prefecture.
s0123.idiomatic: Yizhou was placed under Pansha Prefecture.

s0124.literal: On guiwei day, an edict addressed the civil officials under the Western Xia Circuit Intendant and Surveillance Commission, forbidding monks from illegally occupying civilian farmland.
s0124.idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict directed Western Xia's surveillance officials over civil administrators to forbid monks from illegally occupying civilian farmland.

s0125.literal: On renchen day, the regulations for rewards and punishments in promoting agriculture and sericulture were clarified.
s0125.idiomatic: On renchen day regulations for rewarding and punishing agricultural promotion were clarified.

s0126.literal: An edict ordered tuotuohesun established on every route.
s0126.idiomatic: An edict ordered relay inspectors (tuotuohesun) established on every route.

s0127.literal: Twelfth month, bingchen new moon; the Directorate of Agriculture was changed to the Grand Directorate of Agriculture, with four additional Traveling Agricultural Promotion Commissioners and four deputies added, and Censorate Vice Director Boluo was made concurrent Grand Director of Agriculture.
s0127.idiomatic: On the bingchen new moon of the twelfth month the Directorate of Agriculture was upgraded to the Grand Directorate of Agriculture, with four additional traveling agricultural promotion commissioners and four deputies; Censorate Vice Director Boluo was also made grand director of agriculture.

s0128.literal: Antong said that Boluo's concurrent appointment as a censorate official had no precedent.
s0128.idiomatic: Antong observed that Boluo's concurrent appointment as both a censorate official and agricultural director had no precedent.

s0129.literal: An imperial directive stated: "Agricultural affairs are no small matter; I understand this deeply — let Boluo oversee them."
s0129.idiomatic: An imperial directive read, "Agricultural affairs are no small matter; I understand this well — let Boluo take overall charge."

s0130.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhao Liangbi of Shaanxi and other routes was made Director of the Imperial Library and appointed State Envoy to Japan.
s0130.idiomatic: Zhao Liangbi, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and other routes, was made director of the imperial library and appointed state envoy to Japan.

s0131.literal: An edict ordered annual sacrifice to the Grand Community Altar, the Grand Grain Altar, and the Wind, Rain, and Thunder Lords.
s0131.idiomatic: An edict ordered annual sacrifices to the Grand Community Altar, the Grand Grain Altar, and the Wind, Rain, and Thunder Lords.

s0132.literal: On wuxu day, more than eighteen hundred newly resettled households from Huaimeng were moved to settle west of the river.
s0132.idiomatic: On wuxu day more than eighteen hundred newly resettled households from Huaimeng were relocated west of the Yellow River.

s0133.literal: On renyin day, the rank of Censor-in-Chief was raised to second grade.
s0133.idiomatic: On renyin day the censor-in-chief's rank was raised to second grade.

s0134.literal: Shaozhou in Henan was reduced to Mianchi County.
s0134.idiomatic: Shaozhou in Henan was downgraded to Mianchi County.

s0135.literal: Zhu Xisu, military commissioner of Song Chongqing, sent spies bearing letters and placards to induce Pacification Commissioner Zhang Dayue and others; Dayue did not break the seals and sent the spies together with their documents to the Eastern Sichuan Military Command.
s0135.idiomatic: Zhu Xisu, Song military commissioner of Chongqing, sent spies with letters and placards to win over pacification commissioner Zhang Dayue and others; Dayue left the seals unbroken and sent the spies and their documents to the Eastern Sichuan military command.

s0136.literal: On dingwei day, the chieftains Anuofu, Leding, and Anuzhao of the three tribes of Jinyu and Piaoguo submitted, presenting three tame elephants and nineteen horses.
s0136.idiomatic: On dingwei day chieftains Anuofu, Leding, and Anuzhao of the three Jinyu and Piaoguo tribes submitted, presenting three tame elephants and nineteen horses.

s0137.literal: On jiyou day, Yuy Road Prefect Gao Yuyishi captured a Song spy; an edict rewarded him.
s0137.idiomatic: On jiyou day Yuy Road prefect Gao Yuyishi captured a Song spy and was rewarded by edict.

s0138.literal: On xinyou day, the Directorate of Waterways was placed under the Grand Directorate of Agriculture.
s0138.idiomatic: On xinyou day the directorate of waterways was placed under the grand directorate of agriculture.

s0139.literal: Prince Bohu'er was made chief of the Jarghuchi.
s0139.idiomatic: Prince Bohu'er was made chief of the jarghuchi.

s0140.literal: The Great State-Protecting Benevolent King Temple was built at Gaoliang River.
s0140.idiomatic: The Great State-Protecting Benevolent King Temple was built on the Gaoliang River.

s0141.literal: An edict revised the regulations for Buddhist monastic vestment colors.
s0141.idiomatic: An edict revised regulations for Buddhist monastic vestment colors.

s0142.literal: That year, registered households throughout the realm numbered one million nine hundred twenty-nine thousand four hundred forty-nine.
s0142.idiomatic: That year registered households throughout the realm totaled 1,929,449.

s0143.literal: Former empresses and consorts and the various princes were granted gold, silver, currency, and silk according to the annual custom.
s0143.idiomatic: Former empresses and consorts and the various princes received gold, silver, currency, and silk as in the annual custom.

s0144.literal: Forty-four persons were sentenced to death.
s0144.idiomatic: Forty-four persons were sentenced to death.

s0145.literal: Eighth year, spring, first month, yichou new moon; King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his Secretariat Director Bak Heng and Lang Jiang Cui Youyan to offer congratulations and deliver the annual tribute.
s0145.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the yichou new moon of the first month of spring, King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his secretariat director Bak Heng and lang jiang Cui Youyan with greetings and the annual tribute.

s0146.literal: On bingyin day, the moon transgressed Bi.
s0146.idiomatic: On bingyin day the moon crossed Bi.

s0147.literal: On jimao day, Alihaiya, associate intendant of the Henan Branch Secretariat, was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
s0147.idiomatic: On jimao day Alihaiya, associate intendant of the Henan branch secretariat, was made vice director of the Ministry of Works.

s0148.literal: Central Secretariat officials said: "There was formerly an edict ordering us to deliberate with the Privy Council and Censorate on the garrison-farming fields established by Alibo and others at Nanyang and elsewhere in the Henan Branch Secretariat. We consider that all garrison-farming households are productive commoners from the interior who, moved far away, lose their livelihoods, and should be returned to their original domiciles.
s0148.idiomatic: Central Secretariat officials reported, "We were formerly ordered to consult the Privy Council and Censorate on the garrison-farming fields Alibo and others had set up at Nanyang and elsewhere in Henan. We hold that garrison-farming households are productive inland commoners who lose their livelihoods when moved far away and should be returned to their original domiciles.

s0149.literal: The civilian levies of Nanjing, Nanyang, Guide, and other places should from now on all be converted and paid in grain, stored at convenient nearby locations, to supply food for the Xiangyang army.
s0149.idiomatic: Civilian levies from Nanjing, Nanyang, Guide, and other places should henceforth be converted to grain payments, stored at convenient nearby sites, to feed the Xiangyang army.

s0150.literal: As for the earlier garrison-farming fields, Alibo himself confessed their failure; the prefectures and districts should be ordered to recruit commoners to lease and cultivate them."
s0150.idiomatic: As for the earlier garrison farms, Alibo himself admitted they had failed; local prefectures and districts should recruit civilians to lease and farm them."

s0152.literal: Shi Tianze requested retirement; the request was not granted.
s0152.idiomatic: Shi Tianze asked to retire; the request was denied.

s0153.literal: An edict stated: "When the capital city was earlier built, three hundred eighty-two resident households were moved; calculate their value and compensate them."
s0153.idiomatic: An edict ordered, "When the capital was built earlier, 382 resident households were relocated; calculate fair compensation and pay them."

s0154.literal: Judicial officials of the Privy Council were established.
s0154.idiomatic: Judicial officials were established at the Privy Council.

s0155.literal: Wuduman was dispatched to lead Mongol troops to garrison Tangdang in the west.
s0155.idiomatic: Wuduman was sent to lead Mongol troops garrisoning Tangdang in the west.

s0156.literal: On bingxu day, Goryeo Pacification Commissioner Ahai raided Jin Island; he encountered rebel forces and suffered many losses.
s0156.idiomatic: On bingxu day Goryeo pacification commissioner Ahai raided Jin Island, met rebel forces, and suffered heavy losses.

s0157.literal: Central Secretariat officials said: "Intelligence shows that remaining grain on Jin Island is nearly exhausted; we should attack while they are weak."
s0157.idiomatic: Central Secretariat officials reported, "Intelligence indicates that remaining supplies on Jin Island are nearly exhausted; we should attack while the rebels are weak."

s0158.literal: An edict did not permit this and ordered inspection of strategic points with constant preparedness.
s0158.idiomatic: An edict refused permission and ordered patrols of strategic points with standing readiness.

s0159.literal: On dinghai day, Gu Ruren and Fei Zhengyin wrote state secrets into a letter and plotted to send Cui Jichun, Jia Kaoshan, and Lu Kun into Song territory; when the affair was discovered they were thoroughly investigated. Zhengyin, Ruren, and Jichun all received capital punishment; Kaoshan and Kun were both exiled to distant regions.
s0159.idiomatic: On dinghai day Gu Ruren and Fei Zhengyin put state secrets into writing and plotted to send Cui Jichun, Jia Kaoshan, and Lu Kun into Song territory; when the plot was exposed they were fully investigated. Zhengyin, Ruren, and Jichun were all executed; Kaoshan and Kun were exiled to distant regions.

s0160.literal: An edict stated: "On every route, widows, orphans, the solitary, the aged, and the sick who cannot support themselves shall be given lodging and fuel and grain by the government."
s0160.idiomatic: An edict ordered, "On every route, widows, orphans, the solitary, the aged, and the sick who cannot support themselves shall receive government lodging and provisions."

s0161.literal: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent envoys bearing a memorial requesting marriage for the crown prince Wang Sim.
s0161.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent envoys with a memorial requesting marriage for crown prince Wang Sim.

s0162.literal: An edict forbade frontier generals from accepting bribes to release soldiers and from illegal exactions.
s0162.idiomatic: An edict forbade frontier generals from taking bribes to release soldiers or imposing illegal levies.

s0163.literal: Famine relief was provided to Beijing and Yidu.
s0163.idiomatic: Famine relief was issued to Beijing and Yidu.

s0164.literal: Second month, yimwei new moon; marriage betrothal gifts among the common people were fixed, with distinctions according to rank.
s0164.idiomatic: On the yiwei new moon of the second month marriage betrothal gifts for commoners were regulated, with distinctions by rank.

s0165.literal: On dingyou day, more than twenty-eight thousand commoners of the Central Capital, Zhending, Shuntian, Hejian, and Pingluan were mobilized to build the palace city.
s0165.idiomatic: On dingyou day more than twenty-eight thousand commoners from the Central Capital, Zhending, Shuntian, Hejian, and Pingluan were mobilized to build the palace city.

s0166.literal: On jihai day, transport commissioners on every route were abolished and absorbed into circuit chief commissions.
s0166.idiomatic: On jihai day transport commissioners on every route were abolished and merged into circuit chief commissions.

s0167.literal: The regulations drawn up by the Ministry of Works and submitted by the Ministry were promulgated throughout the realm.
s0167.idiomatic: Regulations drawn up by the Ministry of Works and approved by the Ministry were promulgated throughout the realm.

s0168.literal: The Shaanxi-Sichuan Branch Secretariat was moved to Xingyuan.
s0168.idiomatic: The Shaanxi-Sichuan branch secretariat was moved to Xingyuan.

s0169.literal: On guimao day, Yesudai'er of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat said: "Recently, because of famine, bandits have greatly increased; conspicuous punishment should be added."
s0169.idiomatic: On guimao day Yesudai'er of the Sichuan branch secretariat reported, "Famine has lately brought a great increase in banditry; harsher punishment should be applied."

s0170.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate; Antong held that: "To execute all strong and petty thieves alike would probably not be appropriate.
s0170.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate; Antong argued, "Executing all strong and petty thieves alike would probably be inappropriate.

s0171.literal: Those whose crimes reach death should still await orders as before."
s0171.idiomatic: Cases warranting death should still await imperial approval as before."

s0172.literal: Left Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Zhao Bi, who administered branch ministry affairs in Dongjing and other routes, was made Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
s0172.idiomatic: Zhao Bi, left vice director of the Central Secretariat and administrator of branch ministry affairs in Dongjing and other routes, was made right vice director of the Central Secretariat.

s0173.literal: On jiachen day, six additional Supervising Censors were added.
s0173.idiomatic: On jiachen day six additional supervising censors were appointed.

s0174.literal: Hududar was ordered to carry an edict to win over Pei Zhongsun, remnant of Lin Yan's faction in Goryeo.
s0174.idiomatic: Hududar was ordered to carry an edict winning over Pei Zhongsun, a remnant of Lin Yan's Goryeo faction.

s0175.literal: On yisi day, Baoheding, Regional Commander-in-Chief of Pacification at Dali, Kuokuodai, tutor to the prince, and others conspired to poison the Prince of Yunnan; Huonichi and Cao Zhen exposed the affair. Baoheding, Kuokuodai, Alawading, and Yisufu were all executed; Cao Zhen, Huonichi, and the witnesses were rewarded with gold and silver in varying amounts.
s0175.idiomatic: On yisi day Baoheding, regional commander-in-chief of pacification at Dali, Prince Tutor Kuokuodai, and others conspired to poison the Prince of Yunnan; Huonichi and Cao Zhen exposed the plot. Baoheding, Kuokuodai, Alawading, and Yisufu were all executed; Cao Zhen, Huonichi, and the witnesses were rewarded with gold and silver in varying amounts.

s0176.literal: Three hundred men of the Shazhou and Guazhou falcon offices were conscripted as soldiers.
s0176.idiomatic: Three hundred falconers from Shazhou and Guazhou were conscripted as soldiers.

s0177.literal: On wushen day, an edict promulgated administrative schedules to officials within and without.
s0177.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict issued administrative schedules to officials throughout the realm.

s0178.literal: An edict ordered ten thousand shi of rice purchased in the Uighur markets.
s0178.idiomatic: An edict ordered purchase of ten thousand shi of rice in the Uighur markets.

s0179.literal: On gengxu day, the prohibition on Eastern Sichuan well salt was strictly reinforced.
s0179.idiomatic: On gengxu day the ban on Eastern Sichuan well salt was sharply reinforced.

s0180.literal: On jiwei day, an edict ordered military officers to wear gold and silver tally tokens; those worn by civilian officials and artisans were all confiscated and not issued again.
s0180.idiomatic: On jiwei day military officers were ordered to carry gold and silver tally tokens; tokens held by civilian officials and artisans were confiscated and not reissued.

s0181.literal: An edict ordered that sea-eagle tally tokens use the founding emperor's personal seal.
s0181.idiomatic: An edict required sea-eagle tally tokens to bear the founding emperor's personal seal.

s0182.literal: On gengshen day, Palace Attendant Jiu Zhu, who had long used a comb in service to the Taizu and bound up the hair that fell from it, was ordered to place it in a casket and store it in a side chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0182.idiomatic: On gengshen day Palace Attendant Jiu Zhu, who had long served the Taizu with a comb and preserved the hair that fell from it, was ordered to enshrine the comb in a casket in a side chamber of the imperial ancestral temple.

s0183.literal: An edict stated: "In all lawsuits, those who conceal themselves or falsely accuse others shall be punished with the crime they alleged."
s0183.idiomatic: An edict ordered, "In all lawsuits, those who go into hiding or falsely accuse others shall receive the penalty for the crime they alleged."

s0184.literal: Guide was divided out as a separate prefecture, and Su, Bo, Pi, and Xu prefectures were detached and placed under it.
s0184.idiomatic: Guide was made a separate prefecture, with Su, Bo, Pi, and Xu detached and placed under it.

s0185.literal: Shen Prefecture was promoted to Nanyang Prefecture, and Tang, Deng, Yu, Song, and Ru were detached and placed under it.
s0185.idiomatic: Shen Prefecture was elevated to Nanyang Prefecture, with Tang, Deng, Yu, Song, and Ru placed under it.

s0186.literal: Famine relief was provided to Xijing.
s0186.idiomatic: Famine relief was issued to Xijing.

s0187.literal: Third month, yichou day; the Hedong-Shanxi Circuit Surveillance Commission was expanded, the Hedong-Shaanxi Circuit was changed to the Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit, and the Northern Mountains East-West Circuit was changed to the Northern Mountains Liaodong Circuit.
s0187.idiomatic: On yichou day in the third month the Hedong-Shanxi surveillance commission was expanded, the Hedong-Shaanxi circuit was renamed Shaanxi-Sichuan circuit, and the Northern Mountains East-West circuit was renamed Northern Mountains Liaodong circuit.

s0188.literal: An edict stated: "At New Year's Day, the imperial birthday, and court assemblies, all officials' memorials, foreign tribute, envoys' audience and farewell ceremonies shall fall under the Ceremonial Protocol Office."
s0188.idiomatic: An edict ordered, "At New Year's Day, the imperial birthday, and court assemblies, all officials' memorials, foreign tribute, and envoys' audience and farewell ceremonies shall be handled by the Ceremonial Protocol Office."

s0189.literal: On bingzi day, the Salt Revenue Chief Transport Commissions of the Shandong, Hejian, and Shaanxi circuits were changed to Chief Salt Transport Commissions.
s0189.idiomatic: On bingzi day the salt revenue chief transport commissions of Shandong, Hejian, and Shaanxi circuits were renamed chief salt transport commissions.

s0190.literal: On yimao day, Central Secretariat officials said: "The Goryeo rebel Pei Zhongsun asks that the armies withdraw their camps and then he will submit;
s0190.idiomatic: On yimao day central secretariat officials reported, "The Goryeo rebel Pei Zhongsun asks that our armies withdraw before he submits;

s0191.literal: Xindu did not accede to his request, and now he wishes to receive Jeolla Circuit to dwell in and be directly subject to the court."
s0191.idiomatic: Xindu did not grant his request, and now he wishes to receive Jeolla Circuit to live in and come directly under the court."

s0192.literal: An edict, regarding his evasive words and months of delay, did not grant this.
s0192.idiomatic: An edict, citing his evasive language and months of delay, refused.

s0193.literal: On xinsi day, Xiayi County was restored, with Dangshan incorporated into it.
s0193.idiomatic: On xinsi day Xiayi County was restored, with Dangshan incorporated into it.

s0195.literal: Han Shi'an, wanhu of Bin-Di, was charged with privately storing grain, burning military equipment, falsely using relay horses, and on his own authority requesting Prince Tachar's allotment of four counties in Yidu, and other matters; the responsible offices repeatedly reported this. An edict ordered his execution and confiscation of his household property.
s0195.idiomatic: Han Shi'an, wanhu of Bin-Di, was charged with hoarding grain, destroying military equipment, falsely using relay horses, and on his own authority requesting Prince Tachar's allotment of four Yidu counties, among other offenses; responsible offices had repeatedly reported him. An edict ordered his execution and confiscation of his property.

s0196.literal: On jiashen day, the imperial carriage went to Shangdu.
s0196.idiomatic: On jiashen day the Emperor went to Shangdu.

s0197.literal: On yiyou day, Xu Heng, citing old age and illness, resigned secretariat duties; he was made Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and Director of the Imperial University. Heng returned his old salary, and an edict separately granted the new salary.
s0197.idiomatic: On yiyou day Xu Heng resigned secretariat duties citing old age and illness; he was made chancellor of the imperial academy and director of the imperial university. Heng returned his old salary, and an edict granted a new salary separately.

s0198.literal: An order established the National University, adding one Vice Director, one Erudite, and one Assistant Erudite each, and selecting sons and grandsons of Mongol and Han officials attending court and of their close attendants, together with outstanding youths, as students.
s0198.idiomatic: An order established the national university, adding one vice director, one erudite, and one assistant erudite each, and selecting as students the sons and grandsons of Mongol and Han officials at court and of close attendants, together with outstanding youths.

s0199.literal: On dinghai day, Mars transgressed the Western Rampart General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
s0199.idiomatic: On dinghai day Mars crossed the Western Rampart General in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

s0200.literal: On jichou day, the Western Xia Zhongxing Branch Secretariat and other routes were established, with Chanhai made Associate Administrator of Branch Ministry Affairs.
s0200.idiomatic: On jichou day the Western Xia Zhongxing branch secretariat and other routes were established, with Chanhai made associate administrator of branch ministry affairs.
